production.note: BMW Group Classic: 'Production 09/2002 - 01/2004', 1,383 built. Customer series production is usually dated to 2003 only - see discrepancies.

body.note: 2 doors / 4 seats; CSL stands for 'Coupé, Sport and Lightweight'.

drivetrain.note: The press kit does not spell out the drive layout; its spec table gives a single final drive (3.62:1) with M differential lock. The CSL is a version of the E46 M3, which BMW's US spec sheet describes as 'Front engine/rear drive'.

transmission.note: 'Exclusively' the six-speed Sequential M Gearbox with Drivelogic (SMG II); no conventional manual was offered.

powerHp.note: 265 kW / 360 PS at 7,900 rpm (BMW's English text prints '360 bhp'); 360 PS x 0.98632 = 355 hp.

weightLb.note: 1,385 kg DIN x 2.20462 = 3,053 lb (BMW's own rounding prints 3,054 lb). Only one configuration. EU weight including 75 kg for driver and luggage is 1,460 kg.

sources.title: The New BMW M3 CSL (press kit, 3/2003)
BMW E46 M3 CSL - The Best Performance Car BMW Has Ever Built?

discrepancies.reason: DIN vs EU weight. 1,460 kg is the EU figure (DIN plus 75 kg for driver and luggage); 1,385 kg is DIN. The press kit's spec table labels 1,385 kg as 'EU' with that footnote, but its text and its 'power-to-weight ratio to DIN' of 5.2 kg/kW (1,385 / 265) show 1,385 kg is the DIN figure, and 1,385 + 75 = 1,460.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 1,385 kg DIN (3,053 lb), per the guide's DIN rule.

discrepancies.reason: BMW Group Classic's range appears to include pre-series cars; BMWBLOG counts customer series production only (and gives 1,358 units against BMW's 1,383).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the manufacturer's dates (2002-2004), flagged for review.

reviewNotes: Production years: BMW Group Classic says 09/2002 - 01/2004, but series production for customers is widely given as 2003 only; decide whether the clue should read 2002-2004 or 2003-2004/2003. Drivetrain (RWD) is not stated in words by any page opened for this car; it is taken from the press kit's single final drive and the standard E46 M3's 'rear drive' layout.
